exposure: Birth at or after 41 weeks gestation (7 or more days after due date)
cohort: The study included 4,036,346 singleton infants born in Sweden between 1973 and 2012.
finding: Singleton infants born at or after 41 weeks gestation had a higher risk of developing neonatal encephalopathy, with the risk increasing by an estimated 20% per week after the due date, and this association was more marked in older mothers.
gest_age: The study focused on birth at or after 41 weeks gestation as the primary exposure, within a larger cohort of infants born between 1973 and 2012.
